classes.same-value: at the only input where the mutated test decides differently, both arms compute the same thing: an equal value written over itself, a block copied onto itself, a clamp that changes nothing at its boundary, a lock flag already unlocked, a prefix written the same either way.
classes.unreachable-input: the mutation differs only for an input this code cannot be handed: a core id at or past the core count, a command id of zero, the slot of an idle task (idle tasks are never deleted), a zero-length message stored, a name longer than the validation window, a zero-core configuration (refused).
classes.unused-value: the mutated value is never read on the path it is computed for.
classes.redundant-guard: the same condition is decided again where it matters -- the C's own double sampling, a frame that end_wait has already cleared, an arm the caller's context makes false -- so the mutated guard only moves where the answer is reached.
classes.fast-path: the guard chooses a short path whose answer the long path also gives; it exists for speed.
classes.c-undefined: differs only for input the C configASSERTs against (event bits in the control byte, a mutex holder deleted while it holds), where FreeRTOS has no defined answer.
classes.interrupt-window: differs only if an interrupt lands between two reads inside one call; the oracles deliver interrupts between calls (as reasons.json's class of the same name).
classes.yield-window: two cores: differs only while a core asked to yield has not yet taken it; every harness takes a requested yield at the end of the step that asked (as reasons.json).
classes.pre-scheduler: differs only before the scheduler starts, which no compared run steps through (as reasons.json).
classes.same-code: the mutated test only chooses between two copies of the same code -- a body in line and the same body out of line, kept apart for speed -- so either arm does exactly what the other does.
